name: Stylized frag launcher explosion (18-layer stack)

source.title: Stylized Frag Launcher Explosion, Overwatch inspiration (realtimevfx forum breakdown)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: nothing but the projectile arriving; the hit is instant so the first frame is the flash

phases.name: release
phases.what: flash lasting 2-3 frames, shockwave light fill and burst core fire in the same instant, each offset by only 2-3 frames

phases.name: impact
phases.what: core gas pushes out and brakes to a halt, thin ring races outward and dissolves, sparks fly

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: dark brown smoke is the only thing left and lingers longest

layers.motion: scale pop 0.3 to 1.6 over 3 frames then cut
layers.notes: very short on purpose; the artist stresses that the 2-3 frame life is what makes it punchy

layers.motion: flat disc, fast expand, soft-edged mask, dissolves while growing
layers.notes: reads as the first background fill of light; no flipbook needed, a radial gradient mask is enough

layers.motion: radial burst from centre, drag 4-6, gravity 0, fade before fully stopped
layers.notes: the burst core: high drag so particles decelerate hard and hang in the air

layers.motion: radial burst, stretched along velocity, drag 1.5, gravity 5
layers.notes: two flavours spawned together: trailed ones and stretched ones; lifetime ends just after the ring is gone

layers.motion: slow rise, drag 2, growing, long fade
layers.notes: starts almost at once but outlives everything; sits behind the bright layers

layers.motion: intensity spike then exponential decay over 0.5s
layers.notes: a point light flash makes the ground react

layers.motion: 0.25s decaying shake
layers.notes: short and sharp, matches the flash length

whyItLooksGood: Layers start only a few frames apart, so the blast feels layered in time rather than a single sprite
Fast layers are short, the dull smoke is long, so the eye gets bright then settles
Drag on the core makes the gas feel heavy instead of drifting away
buildNotes: Build as six groups with explicit start offsets of 0, 0.03, 0.06 s. Flash = additive glow sphere that scales up and dies in 0.05 s. Ring = flat ground ring with a soft radial mask that grows and thins. Core and sparks from one Emitter burst, core with drag ~5, sparks with gravity and velocity-stretched quads. Smoke is a normal-blend emitter drawn first (render order behind). Exaggerate: hold the flash a frame longer, double the spark count, add a second thin ring 0.08 s later, add instanced debris chunks, and a 1-frame white screen flash.

name: Arcane-style purple 2D/3D hybrid blast

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: small pulse that sucks in, hand-drawn style shapes rotate

phases.name: release
phases.what: painted flash plus the first rotating shell snaps outward

phases.name: impact
phases.what: stacked rotating 3D shells and flat painterly sprites expand and distort

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: violet wisps and dim embers dissipate

layers.motion: pulse in, radius 0.3 to 0.15 then pop
layers.notes: tiny compression before release sells the force

layers.motion: 2-frame hold then shrink
layers.notes: hard-edged, painterly shape rather than a soft blob, helps the 2D-in-3D feel

layers.motion: open shell mesh rotating on two axes, scale up with ease-out, dissolve via noise threshold
layers.notes: the artist explicitly set up rotation as its own step; give each shell a different spin speed

layers.motion: flat ring, ease-out growth
layers.notes: ties the blast to the ground

layers.motion: outward drift with swirl noise, drag 2, low gravity -0.5
layers.notes: stepped-looking sprite animation (low framerate) keeps the hand-drawn look

layers.motion: expanding refraction ring
layers.notes: subtle, helps the shell read as volume

whyItLooksGood: Mixing flat painted shapes with 3D shells gives a unique, non-generic silhouette
A single saturated hue with only a white-hot core keeps it iconic
Rotation on several axes makes simple shapes feel complex
buildNotes: Use 2-3 additive hemisphere/open-cylinder meshes with a noise-threshold dissolve shader, each rotating at a different rate and scaling with easeOutCubic. Draw sprites at 12 fps stepping for the hand-drawn feel. Stay in one hue, white only in the core. Exaggerate: add a second contrasting shell in pink, longer dissolve trails, bigger chromatic offset on distortion, and a brief full-screen violet tint.

name: Ground slam shockwave with lingering range ring

source.title: DuranPhysics sketch, ground ring feedback (realtimevfx forum)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: dust drawn in, ground telegraph circle brightens

phases.name: release
phases.what: HDR flash on impact point, ring born

phases.name: impact
phases.what: shockwave ring expands to full range, dust and rocks thrown out

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: ring lingers to show the radius, cracks and dust settle

layers.motion: range circle fades in, pulses once
layers.notes: forum advice: let the ring stay a moment so the spell range is readable

layers.motion: brief HDR boost (intensity x3) for 3 frames
layers.notes: the short over-bright pulse on impact was a specific recommended fix

layers.motion: ease-out expand to the damage radius, thickness shrinking
layers.notes: ring edge should match the true hit radius

layers.motion: radial low ring, drag 3, slight rise
layers.notes: dust hugging the ground, tinted to the surface

layers.motion: instanced rocks, velocity up and out, gravity 14, random spin
layers.notes: contextual debris and cracks add weight

layers.motion: crack decal stays, fades over 1s
layers.notes: scar sells the aftermath

layers.motion: 0.3s decaying
layers.notes: pair with the flash

whyItLooksGood: The lingering ring turns a pretty effect into readable gameplay information
An over-bright first frame creates impact before anything else is visible
Ground cracks give an aftermath beat
buildNotes: Flat ring mesh with radial mask shader whose radius uniform equals gameplay radius. Hold at full radius for 0.4 s before fading. Flash = glow sphere intensity 3x for 3 frames. Instanced debris with gravity, dust emitter with high drag at ground level. Exaggerate: double ring (a fast thin one and a slow thick one), taller dust curtain, longer shake, and rocks that bounce.

name: Layered fireball projectile with rock core and flame shell

source.title: How to design and animate a fireball VFX in Unreal Engine 5 (80.lv)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: small burst at the caster, fireball spawns

phases.name: release
phases.what: fireball travels with a fire tail, sparks and a shell around a core

phases.name: impact
phases.what: collision triggers a separate burst system

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: trail particles finish their lifetimes

layers.motion: slowly rotating rock sphere at the centre
layers.notes: dark core gives contrast so the fire reads bright

layers.motion: outer shell mesh with scrolling distorted noise and dissolve, counter-rotating
layers.notes: shell is the main fire read; use two opposing meshes so the texture shows from both sides

layers.motion: flame sprites trailing behind, small at birth and death, large at mid-life, drag 1
layers.notes: size and alpha curves are what make the tail billow rather than pop

layers.motion: short-lived front sparks with strong curl-noise swirl, plus a trail of sparks with random sizes
layers.notes: two separate sets: one jittery at the head, one left behind

layers.motion: constant halo, 1.5x core size
layers.notes: high emissive value (about 8x) so bloom picks it up

layers.motion: pop and shrink in 0.1s
layers.notes: separate impact system on collision

layers.motion: slow expansion, drag 2
layers.notes: leave a trail of darkness behind the fire

whyItLooksGood: Dark rock core contrasts with the additive flame shell
Randomized lifetime, size and rotation prevents visible repetition
Distortion plus dissolve on the same noise gives flowing fire without a flipbook
Dark and ice variants were made by only recolouring and slowing, so the structure is reusable
buildNotes: Core: dark icosphere. Shell: slightly larger icosphere with a shader that offsets UVs by noise and thresholds the same noise for dissolve; add a second copy rotating the other way. Tail: Emitter with drag 1, spawn rate 80/s, size curve 0.3 to 1 to 0, alpha in/out. Sparks: two emitters, one orbiting the head, one dropped on the path. Halo: glow sphere with emissive 8. For variants swap palette (violet/black for dark, cyan for ice with slower speed). Exaggerate: longer tail, double sparks, ground light that travels with the ball.

name: Realistic seeking fireball with ribbon tail and random arcs

source.title: VFX for Games Tutorial 03: Realistic Fireball Projectiles (JangaFX, realtimevfx)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: ball ignites at spawner

phases.name: release
phases.what: ball curves toward the target on a randomized arc, leaving ribbon fire, smoke and sparks

phases.name: impact
phases.what: hit on target

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: tail smoke dissipates

layers.motion: leading hot core
layers.notes: the leading projectile element is the brightest, smaller than the tail

layers.motion: ribbon following the ball, width tapering to zero, UV scroll with dissolve
layers.notes: fire trail built as a ribbon, not as particles

layers.motion: left behind, expanding, drag 2, slight rise
layers.notes: smoke is a separate emitter with its own dissolve; the author found dissolve preview with a levels adjustment useful for finding stuck bright patches

layers.motion: small, shed from head with random velocity, gravity 3
layers.notes: adds speed cues

layers.motion: short pop
layers.notes: keep impact fast

whyItLooksGood: Randomized arc paths mean multiple casts never look identical
Arc offset grows then shrinks over the first second, so it homes in on the target in a natural curve
Ribbon trail connects the ball to its path
buildNotes: Position = lerp(start, target, ease(t)) + perpendicular offset * sin(PI * t) * randomAmplitude (axis chosen randomly per cast, offset only during the first second). Feed the head position to a trail-ribbon with tapering width. Add smoke emitter at 40/s. Seed amplitude per cast. Exaggerate: wider arcs, add a second ball in the volley with different amplitude, make the ribbon longer than seems reasonable, and hot-white core.

name: Procedural electric orb projectile

source.title: Tutorial: Creating Electric Orbs in Unity (80.lv, Gabriel Aguiar)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: orb crackles into existence

phases.name: release
phases.what: orb flies with arcing strands that flicker

phases.name: impact
phases.what: burst of branching arcs

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: sparks and afterglow

layers.motion: core with fresnel rim, pulsing 12Hz
layers.notes: the orb is built with a procedural shader on a 3D mesh, so it needs no texture painting

layers.motion: shell of noise-driven strands wrapping the sphere, reseeded every 2-3 frames
layers.notes: the step-seeded flicker is what makes it feel electric

layers.motion: shed from the surface, short life, drag 1, no gravity
layers.notes: tiny and fast

layers.motion: thin jagged ribbon behind
layers.notes: jitter vertices each frame

layers.motion: pop and 3-4 radiating arcs
layers.notes: arcs reuse the same strand shader

whyItLooksGood: A shader-built orb stays crisp at any scale
Flicker at low update rate (not smooth) reads as electricity
White core with a cool rim keeps contrast
buildNotes: Sphere mesh with fresnel shader; animate strands by noise on view-angle and reseed time in steps of 1/20 s. Generate lightning-arc segments on a sphere (random great-circle arcs with jitter) and regenerate every 3 frames. Sparks emitter small. Exaggerate: bigger rim glow, more strands, brief bloom spike when changing seeds, and blue-violet afterimage at impact. Note: the source page was thin, so details are the standard approach to a procedural orb, not verified numbers.

name: Niagara meteor strike (shell, flash, burst, scorch)

source.title: Real-time meteor strike, UE 5.6 Niagara (The Rookies project)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: meteor descends wrapped in a burning shell

phases.name: release
phases.what: contact flash

phases.name: impact
phases.what: sparks, dust shockwave and rocks burst out

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: scorch mark and debris stay on the ground

layers.motion: rock mesh, tumbling, falling on a diagonal
layers.notes: main meteor body

layers.motion: three emitters: hot flame skin, ember shed, trailing fire; drag 1, velocity opposite travel
layers.notes: the shell is three emitters, not one

layers.motion: long trail along the path, expanding
layers.notes: visible trajectory helps the player read where it lands

layers.motion: pop on contact
layers.notes: separate from the burst

layers.motion: radial burst, gravity 8, stretched
layers.notes: one of three burst emitters

layers.motion: low expanding dust ring
layers.notes: dust shockwave emitter

layers.motion: scattered rocks, collide with ground, gravity 14
layers.notes: only these need collision; everything else is non-colliding to save cost

layers.motion: scorch fades in, embers glow in it for 1s
layers.notes: two ground-mark emitters: scorch and debris

layers.motion: 0.5s decaying
layers.notes: heavy

whyItLooksGood: Clear sequence: fall, flash, burst, scar
Several small emitters for one part gives richer shell than one big sprite
Aftermath stays in the world, so impact has weight
buildNotes: Spawn the rock 40 units up and 25 sideways, falling over 1.2 s with ease-in. Shell = 3 emitters attached to the rock. On y=0 contact: flash (0.1 s), burst (sparks, dust ring, instanced rocks), scorch decal that fades over 4 s, shake 0.5 s. Show a ground telegraph during the fall. Exaggerate: bigger rock, a double flash, a low-frequency shake, rocks that bounce, and a column of dust that rises.

name: Flamestrike ground fire with circle and cracks

source.title: Sarah Carmody, World of Warcraft Legion reel 2016 (realtimevfx forum thread)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: arcane circle appears; commenters wished for a pulse or ground glow here

phases.name: release
phases.what: fire erupts instantly, because damage lands on frame 0

phases.name: impact
phases.what: columns of flame roil across the circle

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: cracked, glowing ground and embers remain

layers.motion: draws in and rotates slowly, brightens on trigger
layers.notes: the circle shape tells the damage area

layers.motion: ground pulse 0.2s before eruption
layers.notes: the forum's suggestion to restore anticipation

layers.motion: tall flame columns rising, scrolling noise, dissolve at top; many at random positions inside the radius
layers.notes: bright inside, darker edges

layers.motion: rise with turbulence, gravity -3, drag 1
layers.notes: embers add height

layers.motion: slow rise
layers.notes: keeps the scene dark and the fire contrasty

layers.motion: cracks glow orange then cool to black over 1.5s
layers.notes: praised in the thread: cracks make the aftermath feel strong

layers.motion: flickering orange point light
layers.notes: shifts at random 10Hz

whyItLooksGood: Immediate impact respects gameplay but a ground pulse still gives the eye a tell
The cracks glowing then cooling gives time-based storytelling
Several flame columns at random heights vary silhouette
buildNotes: Rune circle ring mesh + a pulse (scale 1.0 to 1.05, bright) 0.15 s before the columns. Spawn 12-20 light-pillar columns with random height 2-5 and 0.1 s stagger. Scrolling-noise shader with vertical gradient. Cracks: radial crack decal with emissive that interpolates orange to black. Exaggerate: taller columns, white-hot core, big ember count, a short screen vignette of orange.

name: Ice spike eruption with fog, snow and ground frost

source.title: Ice Spikes VFX production tips and tricks (80.lv)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: tiny snow burst and frost starts to spread

phases.name: release
phases.what: main spikes thrust up in a wave, floor lifts slightly after them

phases.name: impact
phases.what: floor breaks apart, shards and fog burst, camera shake

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: spikes stay, cold fog lingers, frost decal grows

layers.motion: frost grows outward from the centre via sphere mask
layers.notes: decal radius driven by a growing sphere mask

layers.motion: modular spike meshes, wave-like rise with per-group offset so they do not move in unison, ease-out overshoot
layers.notes: icy shader with a bright rim and a second large normal-like detail layer

layers.motion: floor chunks and shards, gravity 12, spin
layers.notes: floor delays slightly so it rises with the spikes' main motion

layers.motion: chill fog puffs, expand, drag 2, vary per sprite
layers.notes: each puff has random offset so they differ

layers.motion: snow and shards drifting down with swirl, gravity 0.5
layers.notes: snow burst accents the start and a light emitter lingers after
built around the core explosion beat

whyItLooksGood: Core beat first, then everything else is timed around it
Offsets between spike groups make a travelling wave instead of one pop
Lingering cold fog and growing decal give a clear aftermath
buildNotes: Cone/prism meshes with a rim-light + fresnel material; stagger spawn by distance from centre (0.03 s per unit), each scaling y from 0 with easeOutBack. Floor shards as instanced debris. Fog as 20 big low-alpha sprites. Frost decal as ring mask growing to radius. Exaggerate: taller central spike, spikes in 2-3 sizes, white flash at the base, glittering sparkles on the spike tips.

name: Lightning strike beam with endpoint-driven impact

source.title: VFX breakdown: fire and lightning spell in UE4 (80.lv)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: tiny spark at start

phases.name: release
phases.what: all layers fire on the same delay value

phases.name: impact
phases.what: beam flickers, smoke and embers burst at the endpoint

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: glow mark and debris settle

layers.motion: ribbon between points, colour shifts along its length, width varies
layers.notes: driven by a user-set endpoint

layers.motion: jagged re-seeded path every 2 frames, thin branches
layers.notes: adds crackle on top of the beam

layers.motion: puffs at the endpoint, sprite warped by noise driven by age
layers.notes: smoke warping with age avoids static puffs

layers.motion: burst from endpoint, gravity 6, drag 1
layers.notes: embers start where the endpoint lands

layers.motion: hit mark flash then fade
layers.notes: glowing hit mark

layers.motion: small ground chunks, gravity 12
layers.notes: ground debris

layers.motion: 1-2 frames
layers.notes: lightning is instantaneous

whyItLooksGood: Everything fires on one delay, which is how lightning feels (instant)
Colour changes along the beam length keep it interesting
Endpoint-driven emitters tie the sky to the ground
buildNotes: Beam = ribbon of 12-20 jittered points; regenerate jitter every 0.03 s, 3 frames. Drive impact emitters from the endpoint vector. Flash on frame 0, hold for 0.15 s with flicker, then fade parts at different rates. Exaggerate: wider white core, extra branching, 2-frame screen flash, scorch decal and a small shockwave ring.

name: Channeled beam with matched hand and target effects

source.title: World of Warcraft VFX overview from Luis Aguas (80.lv)

phases.name: release
phases.what: beam connects

phases.name: impact

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: beam retracts, residual wisps

layers.motion: pulsing orb in the hand
layers.notes: hand effect mirrors the target effect to visually connect them

layers.motion: scrolling noise along length, slight sine wobble
layers.notes: dark base colour with cyan accents is the style used in the Drustvar witch magic

layers.motion: thin twisting ribbons orbiting the main beam
layers.notes: gives the beam body

layers.motion: particles streaming along the beam, drag 0.5
layers.notes: shows direction of flow

layers.motion: impact sprite mirroring the hand glow, flicker
layers.notes: matching hand and impact makes caster and target feel linked

layers.motion: sprays from the impact
layers.notes: keeps the endpoint busy

whyItLooksGood: Three linked parts: hand, beam, impact, with matching look
Dark base layer with cyan accents makes brighter parts pop
Darker elements sit behind brighter ones
buildNotes: Beam = camera-facing ribbon from hand to target, recomputed each frame. Render order: dark wide ribbon (normal blend), then bright narrow additive core, then orbiting ribbons. Hand glow and impact glow share the same sprite and colour. Exaggerate: pulse the width at 6 Hz, add a lens-flare sprite at the hand, add small shake while channelling, and sparks that fly along the beam.

name: Charged energy beam: charge, launch, blast and dispersal

source.title: Creating a Charged Energy Beam in Unreal Engine (Gnomon Workshop, Raul Ruiz)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: energy gathers into a growing orb at the muzzle

phases.name: release
phases.what: beam launches

phases.name: impact
phases.what: beam holds, blast at the target

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: dispersal and glow fade

layers.motion: particles pulled inward to the muzzle, accelerating, negative drag
layers.notes: inward motion before outward is the classic charge tell

layers.motion: grows with ease-in until launch
layers.notes: growth speed is the build-up

layers.motion: fast scroll, mask falloff at both ends, noise breakup
layers.notes: course covers masks, falloffs, breakup and noise shaping

layers.motion: muzzle flash 0.1s
layers.notes: marks the launch

layers.motion: ring expands at target
layers.notes: blast phase

layers.motion: dispersal, drag 1.5, gravity 2

layers.motion: 2 frames
layers.notes: optional

whyItLooksGood: Long charge builds expectation, short release gives payoff
Falloff mask at beam ends avoids hard geometry edges
Dispersal beat gives the effect a soft end
buildNotes: Charge: emitter with particles spawned on a sphere shell with velocity toward the centre; the glow sphere radius from 0.1 to 0.8 with easeInQuad. Launch: cylinder/ribbon with scrolling noise texture, alpha mask smoothstep at both ends. Blast: ring + sparks + glow at the target. Exaggerate: longer charge with rising pitch cue, camera zoom/pull during the launch, a beam that is 3x too thick for 0.15 s then thins. Only the course overview page was readable, so phase timings are estimates.

name: Flipbook lightning bolt with staged fade

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: swirl and tiny particles around the caster sphere

phases.name: release
phases.what: initial bright flash of the full bolt

phases.name: impact
phases.what: bolt flickers, pieces drop out

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: a frame or two of sparse leftover fragments

layers.motion: source orb with a visible connection to the bolt
layers.notes: feedback: the bolt needs a visible link to where it starts

layers.motion: flipbook-like frames: reroll every 2 frames; start segment straighter, more distortion toward the far end
layers.notes: also remove in-between frames to force flicker with high contrast shapes

layers.motion: chain jump to the next target, 80ms stagger
layers.notes: small fragments fade first, main bolt lasts a few frames longer

layers.motion: burst of dots with strong motion, drag 2
layers.notes: dot motion was praised

layers.motion: flash at each hit
layers.notes: randomize spawn timing: uniform waves look robotic

whyItLooksGood: Fragments fade at different times instead of the whole bolt fading as one
Randomized flash timing breaks mechanical rhythm
A last sparse frame makes the ending feel analog
buildNotes: Segment the bolt into pieces (each with its own life 0.1-0.25 s); fade smaller branches first, trunk lasts 2-3 frames longer. Chain: after the first hit wait 0.08 s +/- 0.03 and spawn the next arc to the nearest enemy. Reroll jitter every 2 frames. Keep the first segment near-straight. Exaggerate: wider bloom, 1-frame white screen flash per jump, thicker trunk for the first 3 frames.

source.title: Electric Blast, Houdini and Niagara (realtimevfx forum)

phases.name: impact

phases.name: aftermath

layers.motion: volumetric main bolt, random rotation per cast so it reads from every angle
layers.notes: overall shape matters more than fine detail

layers.notes: second mesh adds volume, sprites add detail

layers.motion: small masked particles, drag 1

layers.motion: central wave with large-scale noise

Randomized rotation avoids a single flat view

Spawn 6-8 ground branch ribbons radiating on the floor, each with an emissive glow that fades over 1 s. Keep ribbon count low (the author hit 200-500 particles with 10 ribbon tracks). Exaggerate: double the number of ground furrows, add a white-blue flash, glow on all small elements, and floor sparks.

name: Mesh sweep slash with panning texture and lag

source.title: UE4 weapon slash: meshes vs AnimTrail data (realtimevfx forum)

phases.what: sweep mesh snaps in and swings

phases.name: impact
phases.what: hit sparks and flash at the contact point

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: slash arc dissolves from tail to head

layers.motion: thin ribbon off the blade tip
layers.notes: animation trail data gives sections only per animation frame, so keep it a minor layer

layers.motion: flat curved sweep mesh with panning texture, head bright, tail dissolving, lags slightly behind the blade
layers.notes: full control over look at every point; remade if the animation changes

buildNotes: Build a crescent ring segment mesh (inner/outer radius with taper), UV.x along the arc. Shader: pan texture, alpha = smoothstep along UV.x moving with time so the head leads and the tail erodes. Rotate it from -70 to +70 degrees with easeOutExpo in 0.12 s. Hit: streak flash plus 20 stretched sparks. Exaggerate: double arc with an offset second slash, bigger arc radius, hit-stop freeze of 2 frames, chromatic distortion.

buildNotes: Hemisphere with fresnel plus 4 stacked shells (scale 1.00, 1.01, 1.02, 1.03) each scrolling a hex/noise texture at different speed and tint. Particle spawn on dome surface; crystals use a spring toward the caster. Ground ring at base.
